review_candidates.description: About Perimeter The limit on superintelligence (SI) is no longer chips. It's power. New data centers wait years for a grid connection, while the office towers, hotels and hospitals of every major city sit on power they were built for and no longer use. Perimeter Compute is on a mission to put that power to work. We turn basements and mechanical rooms into GPU clusters, and our software links them into one inference network running inside the cities where SI will be used. Building owners earn from space that would otherwise sit idle. Frontier labs and inference providers get capacity without the years-long wait, a few miles from their users instead of a few states away. Perimeter is a small, highly leveraged team that has worked every layer of this problem: building GPU infrastructure at Lambda and HPE, engineering commercial buildings at Tishman Speyer and Trane, and routing inference at Subquadratic. The power is already there. Come build what runs on it. How We Work People make the decisions that matter. Agents do everything else. Agents write and review all of our code. People own the calls that are hard to undo: architecture, product direction, taste, and the frameworks we use to make those calls. Most decisions are two-way doors, so you make the call instead of waiting for one. If you like writing code yourself, you'll hate it here. One owner per outcome. You build it, you run it, you grow it. Roles here are bigger than usual. You'll do work that's normally split across engineering, product, sales and design. You'll work directly with customers to figure out what to build. You own the outcome, so you decide how to get there. If you want a clear ticket and someone else owning the result, this isn't the job. We Keep Reinventing How Software Gets Built. Code is a means to an end, not the end. We question every assumption. "Why?" is the most important question you can ask, and a rule nobody can answer it for gets deleted. How we build is code too. Every week, agents find what slowed us down and ship the fix. If you want a process that stays the same, look elsewhere. We build for agents as much as for people. Agents use our tools, APIs, docs and interfaces too. It isn't done until an agent can use it and recover from its errors without help. Every public API is defined once in code, and everything people and agents read about it is generated from that, so nothing drifts. Agents don't remember rules, so anything that matters is a check that fails, not a line in a doc. Because agents do the work, we can be prescriptive: one way to build things, and every agent follows it. If docs and error messages feel like someone else's job, we're not a fit. About The Role You'll own the layer right above our bare metal: the products customers will rent. Our GPUs are spread across buildings, but customers should rent one cloud: a node failing or a site losing its link is our problem, never theirs. You'll build managed Kubernetes and GPU virtual machines on our own hardware, starting with Kubernetes, then own them as products: their service levels, monitoring, adoption and direction. We're building to the criteria behind the top tier of ClusterMAX, SemiAnalysis's public rating of GPU clouds. You're measured on paying customers and how much of our fleet is ready to rent at the service levels we publish. What You'll Do Stand up managed Kubernetes on our bare metal from scratch, with hosted control planes and the GPU and networking stack customers expect Build GPU virtual machines: whole nodes first, then smaller sizes where customers need them Turn one pool of capacity into reserved, on-demand and spot products, with the quota and preemption rules behind them and the usage records billing is built from Build isolation between customers into everything you ship, to the bar the security team sets and tests Make failures ours, not the customer's: move work off a failing node, and keep workloads running when a site loses its link to our central control plane Make every operation work for agents as well as people, through our API, CLI and agent tools Run what you ship: publish its service levels, get paged when they slip, and roll out Kubernetes and GPU driver upgrades without breaking customer workloads Talk to the developers using it and decide what to build next Good fit if you Have built and run production software that people depend on, and owned it when it broke, whether that took you two years or ten Have run production Kubernetes on bare metal, including provisioning, upgrades and node operations Have debugged GPU failures in production: drivers, Xid errors, NCCL hangs Have working knowledge of KVM/QEMU, KubeVirt and GPU passthrough Have owned a product other developers paid for or depended on, including its service levels Get real results from coding agents on infrastructure, and know which changes a person must check Nice to have Hosted control planes with Gardener or k0smotron Bare-metal provisioning with Ironic, Metal3 and Redfish Network fabrics like Netris or Hedgehog, and BlueField DPUs GPU partitioning: MIG, or NVLink partitions through Fabric Manager Quotas and preemption with Kueue Location Fully remote in the US. Apply anyway. We care more about what you've built and how you think than about checking every box. Please write your answers to the application questions yourself, without AI. After you apply, we'll tell you how to use AI in each interview round. We accept applications for this role on an ongoing basis. Perimeter Compute is an equal opportunity employer.
